stories.body: US envoy Jared Kushner has held rare talks in Egypt with Hamas political chief Khalil al-Hayya before meeting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in an effort to revive a US-backed Gaza roadmap. The plan calls for Hamas and other armed groups to disarm, Israeli forces to withdraw and Gaza to be rebuilt under a civilian Palestinian administration, but Netanyahu has publicly rejected it and insists on verifiable disarmament before any withdrawal. Hamas says it is committed to the roadmap but wants Israel to halt attacks and withdraw to the so-called yellow line before implementation begins. Egypt, Qatar and Turkey have mediated the effort, while several Muslim-majority countries have condemned Israel's rejection of the plan.
stories.headline: Kushner meets Hamas and Netanyahu to push US-backed Gaza peace plan

stories.body: President Donald Trump has ordered the Pentagon to substantially reduce the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises with South Korea, citing his good relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and describing the drills as costly and hostile in their signal to Pyongyang. He said it was too late to cancel the exercises, which were due to begin Monday and had been expected to involve about 18,000 South Korean troops. Seoul said the drills would proceed as scheduled. The move comes despite warnings that scaling back training could weaken deterrence and alliance coordination, particularly as North Korea expands its missile and nuclear programmes and its troops gain battlefield experience from Russia's war in Ukraine.
stories.headline: Trump orders sharp reduction in US-South Korea military drills

stories.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed at least 2,325 people, surpassing the 2,299 deaths recorded during the country's 2018-20 outbreak. Officials reported 4,945 confirmed cases, including 101 detected in the previous 24 hours, with six of the country's 26 provinces affected. The outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo species, is the fastest-growing on record and has no approved vaccine or treatment. Conflict, weak health infrastructure, remoteness and late case detection have complicated containment efforts; the reported fatality rate has risen to about 46%. Experimental vaccines and treatments are being evaluated as global health authorities seek to bring transmission under control.
stories.headline: DR Congo Ebola outbreak becomes the country's deadliest on record

stories.body: Ukraine launched one of its largest long-range drone attacks of the war, according to Russian authorities, with strikes reported around Moscow and a major fire at a Wildberries distribution warehouse near Podolsk. Moscow claimed it had downed 1,478 Ukrainian drones in 24 hours, a figure that could not be independently verified, while officials said at least six people were killed in strikes on the Belgorod region. Russia also struck 13 locations in Ukraine, killing at least seven people and injuring dozens. The exchange highlights the accelerating long-range air war, as Ukraine expands its domestic drone and missile capacity while both countries' air defences face increasing pressure.
stories.headline: Ukraine launches major drone attack on Russia as strikes hit both countries

stories.body: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has ordered the military to prepare a plan to transfer civilian law-enforcement responsibilities for Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank to police. The proposal followed criticism of the army's response to settlers besieging Palestinian families in Qusra. Palestinian Vice-President Hussein al-Sheikh called the move a flagrant violation of international law and a step toward formal annexation. Rights advocates and analysts say shifting authority from the military occupation system to a domestic civilian police force could further erase the legal distinction between Israel and the occupied territory, while strengthening the influence of far-right ministers over policing and settlement policy.
stories.headline: Israel plans to transfer West Bank law-enforcement powers to civilian police

stories.body: Days of storms and record-setting flooding in Indiana have left at least seven people dead, as floodwaters along Indianapolis's White River began to recede and rain eased in parts of the state. Emergency crews have conducted rescues in riverside neighbourhoods, while residents returned to flooded homes and businesses to assess losses. Authorities continue to monitor conditions as the state recovers from the severe weather.
stories.headline: Indiana braces for further rain after deadly flooding and storms

stories.body: A coalition of US states is taking Meta to trial in federal court in Oakland, California, alleging that Facebook and Instagram were deliberately designed to addict children and teenagers and that the company improperly collected data from children under 13. Four states, California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey, are leading the trial, with other states expected to pursue later proceedings. The states seek extensive damages that Meta says could reach $1.4 trillion, as well as changes to product features including like counts, infinite scrolling and push notifications for young users. Meta denies the allegations and says its evidence will demonstrate its longstanding commitment to supporting young people.
stories.headline: States take Meta to trial over alleged social-media harms to children

stories.body: Spain is maintaining its policy toward Morocco despite growing criticism after a mass crossing into Ceuta in late July, when more than 70,000 migrants entered the Spanish enclave and thousands remained afterward. The government says Moroccan cooperation enabled the rapid return of many people and says there is no conclusive evidence that Rabat deliberately facilitated the crisis, though diplomats, former ministers and analysts have called for a firmer response. Between 5,000 and 8,000 migrants are still believed to be in Ceuta, many living in makeshift camps and seeking asylum amid strained services. Aid groups report that large numbers of minors remain outside the city's protection system and that migrants have avoided medical care for fear of deportation.
stories.headline: Ceuta migration crisis strains services as Spain reassesses its approach to Morocco

stories.body: A member of Spain's Military Emergency Unit died when a fire engine overturned during operations against the Las Peñas de Riglos wildfire in Huesca, while three other service members were injured. Two were treated for minor injuries in Jaca and a third was taken to Zaragoza hospital in stable condition. The blaze has burned about 17,500 hectares and forced the evacuation of 19 communities and three campsites, affecting more than 1,000 people. Around 1,000 personnel, including more than 500 members of the Military Emergency Unit, and more than 40 aircraft have been deployed; calmer winds and rainfall offered some relief, although officials said the fire remained difficult.
stories.headline: Military firefighter dies while battling Las Peñas de Riglos wildfire in Huesca

stories.body: Three people, including a minor, were killed and a fourth person was seriously wounded in a shooting in the El Rocío district of Isla Cristina, Huelva. Investigators say two masked people on a motorcycle opened fire before fleeing. The dead were reported to be a woman, her child and the woman's mother. The Civil Guard is investigating and is considering whether the attack was a drug-related settling of accounts connected to earlier violence in Huelva province.
stories.headline: Three people, including a minor, killed in shooting in Isla Cristina

stories.body: Barcelona is marking nine years since the jihadist attacks on La Rambla and in Cambrils, which killed 16 people and left hundreds affected. A memorial, normally held at the Pla de l'Os on La Rambla, will be moved to Plaça de Sant Jaume because of construction work. Government figures show that 232 of 368 people recognised by the courts as victims have received compensation, leaving 136 without payment because they have not been located, have not applied or may be unaware of their rights. Victim advocates have criticised authorities for not doing enough to find survivors and inform them of available assistance.
stories.headline: Spain marks ninth anniversary of Barcelona and Cambrils 17-A attacks

stories.body: Organisers of Barcelona's Gràcia festival are seeking ways to reduce alcohol-related disruption while preserving the celebration's nightlife and financing. Some street committees have stopped selling spirits or alcohol altogether, instead relying on food sales and other fundraising, while others continue selling drinks because bar income pays for decorations and programming. The city has required local convenience stores and 24-hour supermarkets to close by 11pm and is again restricting bars from installing additional temporary counters and beer taps. Festival organisers broadly agree on avoiding the promotion of alcohol, but differ over whether limiting sales can meaningfully curb noise, crowding and public drinking.
stories.headline: Barcelona's Gràcia festival seeks to curb alcohol-fuelled nighttime disruption

stories.body: Barcelona's 2025 municipal register lists 2,328 homes with more than ten people registered at the same address, nearly twice the 1,279 recorded in 2021, illustrating the persistence of overcrowded and substandard housing amid the housing crisis. The figure is slightly below the 2,546 recorded in 2024, and the city cautions that registration data are only a snapshot and may include people who no longer live at an address. Municipal authorities cannot refuse registration simply because a dwelling is overcrowded, while social groups warn that the data likely understate unregistered cases and point to a lack of sufficient housing and homelessness services.
stories.headline: Overcrowded apartments with more than ten registered residents become entrenched in Barcelona

stories.body: Barcelona's Urban Guard has criminally charged two drivers after detecting them travelling at more than 120 km/h on city avenues limited to 50 km/h. One driver was clocked at 125 km/h on Avinguda Meridiana while entering the city on 12 August, and another, driving a foreign-registered vehicle, was caught at 130 km/h on Avinguda Diagonal early on 14 August. The cases occurred during the quieter August holiday period, when reduced traffic can encourage dangerous speeding.
stories.headline: Barcelona police charge two drivers caught above 120 km/h on 50 km/h city roads

stories.body: Storms brought hail, intense rain and strong winds to parts of Catalunya, particularly Girona province, prompting the Catalan civil-protection authority to activate its flood emergency plan. Montblanc recorded 59mm of rain and Sant Gregori 55mm, while hail was reported in Besalú, Arbúcies, Amer and Font-rubí. Firefighters received more than 20 weather-related calls, mostly involving fallen trees and branches, blocked drains and a fallen telephone pole; trees also blocked sections of the AP-7 and C-66. Meteocat issued severe-weather warnings for Girona and Pla de l'Estany, warning of possible large hail, damaging gusts, downbursts and tornadoes.
stories.headline: Storms bring hail, heavy rain and strong winds to parts of Catalunya
